mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, which positively impacts S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns over a 60-day horizon in most cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns remain positive despite unemployment exceeding 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth coupled with low unemployment indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If positive labor indicators do not result in positive S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate in a tightening cycle increases borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive despite rising federal funds rates.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation erodes purchasing power and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If high inflation does not result in negative S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production indicates supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive despite low industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth with weak retail sales indicates economic imbalance, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If conflicting demand signals do not result in negative S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts in early-cycle expansion boost economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If housing growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns.
